lessons.title: God made me to know and love him
lessons.idea: God made each of us to know him, love him and be happy with him forever. He gave us a heart to love.
lessons.question: What do you love to do? How can you do it with love?
lessons.activity: Draw yourself with a heart in the middle. Write, “God made me to love.”
teach: God made us to know him, love him and serve him, and to be happy with him forever (CCC 1, 356, 1721).
Love is why we were made. Connect to children’s loves: family, friends, play.
Reassure children who struggle: God’s love does not depend on being good at things.
talk: What do you love? How can you share it?
What does it mean to be happy with God?
How do you show love to your family?
quiz: God made us to…|Win prizes|Know and love him|Be rich|Be alone|1|CCC 1, 356.
What do we do with our hearts?|Fight|Love|Hate|Hide|1|1 John 4:19.
We will be happy with God…|Never|Only now|For a day|Forever|3|CCC 1721.
lessons.life: Do one loving thing for your family each day this week and tell them, “I did it because God made me to love.”
lessons.saint: Thérèse of Lisieux: she said, “My vocation is love.”
lessons.mem: God is love. (1 John 4:8)
lessons.hook: Ask: “What are you good at? What do you love?” Then say, “God made you to love.”
lessons.assess: Ask: “Why did God make you?”

script.open: Hold up a very nice, plain wooden box with nothing inside, and ask the class, “If I made this box, what is it for? Why did I make it?” (Let them guess: to hold things.) “Everything is made for a reason. Today’s question is a very big one: Why did God make YOU?”
teach: Say: “A very old question, asked of every Catholic child, is: ‘Why did God make you?’ And here is the answer: God made me to know him, to love him, and to be happy with him forever. That is why you are here.”

Say: “God did not make us because he was lonely, or because he needed anything. God is already perfectly happy. He made us because he is good, and goodness wants to share. He wanted to share his love and his happiness with us.”

Say: “He gave you a heart to love. And he gave you a mind, so that you can know him. When you learn about God, you are getting to know him. When you love your family, and love God, you are doing exactly what you were made for. And someday, we hope to be with him in heaven, forever.”
ask: Why did God make you? (To know him, love him and be happy with him.)
What do you think it means to ‘know’ God? (Learn about him, pray, listen.)
What does your heart do? (Loves, feels. Say: “God gave you a heart to love.”)
practice: Give each child paper and crayons.
Say: “Draw yourself in the middle of the page.”
Say: “Now draw a big heart on your chest, because God gave you a heart to love.”
Write on the board: “God made me to love.” Have each child copy it at the bottom.
Let children show a neighbor and say, “God made me to love.”
script.close: Pray the Sign of the Cross. Say: “God, thank you for making me. I want to know you and love you.” Send home: “Ask someone at home, ‘Why did God make you?’”

tryit: Draw a big heart in the middle.
lessons.saintStory:
Thérèse Martin was born in France in 1873. Her mother died when she was only four, and her family and her faith were what she held on to. Even as a little girl she wanted to love God with her whole heart.
When she was fifteen she asked to enter a Carmelite convent, and she became a nun. She did not do big, famous things. She did small things with great love: she smiled at a sister who was hard to get along with, and she did chores without complaining. She wrote, “My vocation is love.” She died of illness at twenty-four.
Thérèse understood why God made her: to know him and love him. Each little kindness we do for love is how we do the same.

lessons.title: God takes care of us
lessons.idea: God our Father takes care of everything he made. He knows each of us by name and gives us what we need.
lessons.question: What do birds and flowers teach us about God?
lessons.activity: Look at pictures of birds and flowers. Thank God for three things he gives.
teach: Matthew 6:25–34: God feeds the birds and clothes the flowers; he will care for us (CCC 301, 305). He knows each of us by name.
God uses people to provide: parents, teachers, farmers.
Be careful with children whose families lack food: speak gently and add that we help one another.
talk: Who gives you food?
How does God take care of the birds?
How can we help someone who is hungry?
quiz: God takes care of…|Only some|Everything he made|Only the strong|Nobody|1|Matthew 6:26.
The birds teach us to…|Run|Fly|Trust God|Sing|2|Matthew 6:26.
We thank God for…|Nothing|Cartoons|Our food|Our shoes only|2|Psalm 136:25.
lessons.life: Say grace and thank the people who made the food.
lessons.saint: Francis of Assisi: he preached to the birds and trusted God’s care.
misc: “If I pray, I always get what I want.”
lessons.mem: Give us this day our daily bread.
lessons.hook: Show a picture of a bird eating seeds. Ask, “Who gives the birds food?”
lessons.assess: Ask children to name three things God gives.

script.open: Scatter some birdseed on a tray or bring a feather and a pressed flower. Say, “Who gives the birds their food? Who makes the flowers grow so beautifully?” Take answers, then say, “Jesus told a story about this, and it has something to say to us.”
teach: Read Matthew 6:26 aloud, slowly: “Look at the birds of the air. They do not plant or harvest, but your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not worth more than they?” Say: “Jesus says that if God feeds the birds, God will take care of you.”

Read Matthew 6:28-29: “Consider the lilies of the field. They do not work or spin, and yet not even Solomon in all his glory was dressed like one of these.” Say: “God dresses the flowers in beautiful colors. He will take care of us, too.”

Say: “God knows you by name. He knows what you need before you ask. In the Our Father we say, ‘Give us this day our daily bread.’ That means: Father, please give us what we need today. And we trust him, so we do not need to worry.”
ask: What did Jesus say about the birds? (God feeds them.)
Who takes care of you? (God, and mom, dad, teachers.)
What does it mean to trust God? (To believe he will take care of us.)
practice: Show pictures of birds, flowers, food, a house and family.
Say: “These are things God gives us.” Point to each one.
Let each child pick three things God gives them and tell their partner.
Then say together: “Thank you, Father, for ____.” Go around so that every child gets a turn.
script.close: Say the grace before meals together. Sign of the Cross. Send home: “At dinner, each person says one thing God gave them today.”

tryit: Look at the birds and flowers.
Name three things God gives you.
lessons.saintStory:
Francis was born in Assisi, Italy, about 1182. His family was rich, and he enjoyed a life of parties and fine clothes. Then he heard Jesus call him, and he gave up everything he had to live in poverty and serve God.
Francis trusted God to take care of him, as the Gospel says that God takes care of the birds. He and his friends owned nothing, and God always gave them what they needed. Stories say that Francis spoke to the birds and that they listened, and he wrote a song to thank God for the sun, the moon and the water.
Francis shows us what Jesus teaches in today’s lesson: if God takes care of the birds and the flowers, he will surely take care of us.

lessons.title: The first sin and God’s promise
lessons.idea: Adam and Eve chose not to listen to God. This was sin. But God promised to send a Savior.
lessons.question: What does God do after Adam and Eve sin?
lessons.activity: Retell with picture cards: God made the garden, the sin, the promise.
teach: Genesis 3: Adam and Eve disobeyed and hid. Sin breaks friendship with God (CCC 397, 399).
God didn’t leave them: he promised a Savior (CCC 410).
Do not use fear: God is the one who looks for them (“Where are you?”).
talk: Why did Adam and Eve hide?
How does God show love after they sin?
What does God promise?
quiz: Adam and Eve…|Obeyed|Built a house|Ran a race|Did not listen to God|3|Genesis 3.
After they sinned, God…|Hated them|Promised a Savior|Forgot them|Left|1|Genesis 3:15.
Sin is…|Being tired|A game|Choosing not to love God|Being small|2|CCC 1850.
lessons.life: If you do something wrong this week, say “I’m sorry” right away instead of hiding.
lessons.saint: Dismas, the good thief: he asked Jesus to remember him and was welcomed.
lessons.mem: God promised to send a Savior.
lessons.hook: Hold a toy broken in two. “What happens when we don’t listen?”
lessons.assess: Ask: “What did God promise?”

script.open: Show an apple on a plate with a note on it that says, “Please don’t eat this.” Say, “Imagine your mom put this here. She said do not touch. What would be hard about that? Today’s story is about two people who had to choose.”
teach: Tell: “God made a beautiful garden and put Adam and Eve in it. They were happy, and God walked with them. God said, ‘You can eat from any tree, but not that one.’ It was a way of showing they trusted him.”

Say: “A sneaky serpent said to Eve, ‘Did God really say that? You will not die. You will be like God.’ Eve and Adam believed him. They took the fruit and ate it. They did not listen to God. That is sin. Sin means choosing to disobey God and not do what he asks.”

Say: “Right away they felt afraid and ashamed, and hid. But God did not give up on them. God called, ‘Where are you?’ And he made a promise: he would send someone who would defeat the serpent and make everything right. That Savior is Jesus. Even in our worst mistakes, God has a plan to save us.”
ask: What did God ask Adam and Eve not to do? (Eat from one tree.)
What did they do when they sinned? (Hid.) What did God do? (Looked for them and made a promise.)
Who is the Savior God promised? (Jesus.)
practice: Prepare three picture cards: the garden, the sin and the promise.
Mix them up on the floor and say: “Let’s put these in order.” Have children place them in order, and tell what happens.
Retell the story together, each child saying one sentence.
End by holding up the promise card and saying, “God promised to send a Savior.”
script.close: Pray: “Thank you, God, for promising a Savior.” Sign of the Cross. Send home: “Tell your family the story of the garden and the promise.”

tryit: Look at the pictures in order.
Tell what happens in each one.
lessons.saintStory:
The Gospel tells us about two men who were crucified next to Jesus. The Church has long called one of them Dismas, and remembers him as the “good thief.”
Dismas had done wrong things in his life. As he hung on the cross, he saw that Jesus was good and had done nothing wrong. He said to the other man, who was making fun of Jesus, “Do you not fear God? We deserve this, but this man has done nothing wrong.” Then he turned and said, “Jesus, remember me when you come into your kingdom.”
Jesus answered, “Today you will be with me in Paradise.” Dismas shows us that even after a big mistake, if we say sorry and trust Jesus, he welcomes us. That is the promise God made right after the first sin.

units.title: Stories of God’s friends
units.eq: How does God keep his promises?

lessons.title: Noah and the ark
lessons.idea: God asked Noah to build an ark. Noah listened and trusted God. God made a promise with the rainbow.
lessons.question: Why did Noah build the ark?
lessons.activity: Build a paper boat. Paint a rainbow and say, “God keeps promises.”
teach: Genesis 6–9: Noah trusted God and built the ark. God promised never again to destroy the earth with a flood (CCC 56–58).
The rainbow is a sign of God’s promise.
Focus on trust and promise, not on destruction.
talk: Why did Noah build a boat?
What did God promise?
When do you keep a promise?
quiz: Noah built…|A house|A tower|A wall|An ark|3|Genesis 6.
God’s sign to Noah was…|A rainbow|A bird|A star|A cloud|0|Genesis 9:13.
God keeps…|No promises|Secrets|His promises|Some promises|2|CCC 56.
lessons.life: Look for a rainbow after rain and say, “God keeps his promises.”
lessons.saint: Noah: a righteous man who walked with God.
lessons.mem: I will remember my covenant. (Genesis 9:15)
lessons.hook: Float a paper boat in water. “Noah built a big boat because he listened to God.”
lessons.assess: Ask: “What did the rainbow mean?”

script.open: Spread out a blue cloth, a small toy boat, and some toy animals two by two. Ask, “What do you think is happening in this picture? Where are all these animals going?” Let children guess.
teach: Tell: “Long ago, people stopped listening to God. But there was one man, Noah, who did listen. God said, ‘Noah, build an ark.’ An ark is a very big boat. Noah had never seen a flood. But he did what God asked.”

Say: “Noah, his wife, his sons and their wives went into the ark, with two of every animal. Then it rained for forty days and forty nights. The ark floated on the water. Everyone inside was safe. God took care of them. After a long time, a dove brought back an olive leaf, which meant the land was dry.”

Say: “Then Noah came out of the ark. God put a rainbow in the clouds and said, ‘This is my promise: never again will a flood destroy the earth.’ The rainbow is God’s sign. Whenever we see one, we can say, ‘God keeps his promises.’”
ask: Why did Noah build an ark? (God told him to.)
How do you think Noah felt when people laughed? (Listen. Say: “He trusted God anyway.”)
What is the sign of God’s promise? (A rainbow.)
practice: Give each child a sheet of paper. Show how to fold it into a boat, or give them a printed boat to color.
Let children paint or color a rainbow across the top of a second page.
Put the boat and rainbow together on the table.
Say together: “God keeps promises.”
script.close: Pray: “Thank you, God, for keeping your promises.” Sign of the Cross. Send home: “Look for a rainbow, and remember God’s promise.”

lessons.saintStory:
The Bible calls Noah a righteous man, which means a person who did what was right and listened to God. He lived at a time when most people had stopped listening to God.
God asked Noah to build a very big boat, an ark, even though there was no rain at all. Noah did it, even if people laughed. He gathered his family and two of every kind of animal into the ark. When the rain came and the flood covered the earth, they were safe inside.
When the waters went down, God set a rainbow in the sky and promised he would never again flood the whole earth. Noah teaches us to trust God and do what he asks, even if it’s hard.

lessons.title: Abraham trusts God
lessons.idea: God asked Abraham to leave home and trust him. God promised him many descendants. Abraham believed.
lessons.question: What does it mean to trust someone?
lessons.activity: Look at the night sky or a picture. Count stars as a way to talk about God’s promise.
teach: Genesis 12 and 15: God called Abraham to a new land and promised many descendants. Abraham believed (CCC 59, 145).
Faith is trusting God even when we cannot see the end.
Abraham is the father of all who believe.
talk: What does it mean to trust?
Whom do you trust?
What did God promise Abraham?
quiz: Abraham trusted…|Gold|God|A map|The king|1|Genesis 12.
God promised Abraham…|A house|Many descendants|A pet|A boat|1|Genesis 15:5.
Faith is…|Knowing everything|Trusting God|Being afraid|Winning|1|CCC 146.
lessons.life: Look at the stars and say, “God, I trust you.”
lessons.saint: Abraham: called the father of faith.
lessons.mem: Abram believed the Lord. (Genesis 15:6)
lessons.hook: Look at the sky or at stars on paper. “Can you count them?”
lessons.assess: Ask: “What did Abraham do when God called?”

script.open: Turn off the lights, shine a flashlight through a pierced cardboard to make “stars” on the ceiling, or show a night sky picture. Say, “How many stars are there? Can anyone count them?” Let them try for a moment.
teach: Tell: “A long time ago there was a man named Abraham. He was old, and he had no children. One day God said, ‘Abraham, leave your home and go to a land I will show you. I will make your family a great people.’ What do you think Abraham did? He listened, and he went.”
Say: “Abraham did not know the way. He did not know what would happen. But he trusted God, and that is called faith. Faith means believing God, even when we cannot see.”

Say: “One night God said, ‘Look up at the stars. Your family will be as many as the stars.’ And the Bible says: ‘Abram believed the Lord.’ God kept his promise, and Abraham’s family grew. Jesus is part of that family. God’s promises always come true.”
ask: What did God ask Abraham to do? (Leave home and trust.)
Did Abraham know where he was going? (No.) Did he go? (Yes.) What do we call that? (Faith, trust.)
When is it hard to trust someone? (Listen. Say: “We can always trust God.”)
practice: Show a picture of a starry sky, or turn off lights and show stars with a flashlight.
Let children count aloud together, until they give up.
Say: “Too many to count! That is how many people God promised Abraham.”
Let each child draw stars on a dark paper with a white or yellow crayon, as many as they like.
script.close: Pray: “God, help me trust you like Abraham.” Sign of the Cross. Send home: “Look at the stars tonight and say, ‘God keeps his promises.’”

tryit: Look at the picture of the stars.
lessons.saintStory:
Abraham was an old man, about seventy-five years old, when God spoke to him. God said, “Leave your country and your family, and go to the land I will show you.” God did not tell him exactly where.
Abraham packed up his family, his animals and his tents, and went, because he trusted God. Years passed and he and his wife Sarah still had no children. One night God took Abraham outside and said, “Look at the sky. Count the stars, if you can. That is how many children you will have.” The Bible says, “Abraham believed the Lord.”
God did keep his promise, with a son named Isaac. Because Abraham trusted God so much, he is called our father in faith. He teaches us to believe God’s promises, even when we do not see how they will come true.

lessons.title: Moses and the Ten Commandments
lessons.idea: God freed his people from slavery through Moses. He gave them the Ten Commandments so they could live as his people.
lessons.question: Who did God send to free his people?
lessons.activity: Make a “stone tablets” craft and learn the first three commandments.
teach: Exodus: God freed his people from slavery and gave the Commandments (CCC 2056, 2060). Rules are for love.
Teach the first three commandments simply: love God, respect his name, keep Sunday holy.
God gave the Law after freeing them, not to earn freedom.
talk: Why did God free his people?
What rules help your family?
How do rules help us love?
quiz: God freed his people through…|David|Moses|Noah|Jonah|1|Exodus 3.
The Ten Commandments teach us to…|Win|Love God and others|Run fast|Hide|1|CCC 2055.
The Israelites crossed…|A river|A desert only|The Red Sea|A lake|2|Exodus 14.
lessons.life: Learn the first commandment: “I am the Lord your God. You shall have no other gods before me.”
lessons.saint: Moses: a shy man whom God used to free his people.
lessons.mem: I am the Lord your God. (Exodus 20:2)
lessons.hook: Hold two paper “tablets.” “God gave Moses ten rules to help his people.”
lessons.assess: Ask: “What did God give Moses? Why?”

script.open: Show two things: a rope (chains) and an open door picture. Say, “A long time ago, some people were stuck like this (rope), and God wanted them to be free like this (open door). Today we’ll find out how God set them free.”
teach: Tell: “The people of God were slaves in Egypt. They worked very hard, and they cried to God for help. God heard them! He called Moses from a burning bush: ‘Moses, I will send you to Pharaoh to set my people free.’ Moses was afraid, but God said, ‘I will be with you.’”

Say: “After many signs, Pharaoh let them go. God led them through the sea and out of Egypt. They were free! Then they came to a mountain called Sinai, and God gave Moses ten rules, the Ten Commandments, written on two tablets of stone.”

Say: “The commandments are God’s way of saying, ‘I love you, and here is how to live well.’ The first three are about loving God: 1. I am the Lord your God; you shall have no other gods before me. 2. Do not use God’s name badly. 3. Keep Sunday holy. God’s rules help us love him and each other.”
ask: Who did God choose to lead his people? (Moses.)
What did God give Moses at the mountain? (The Ten Commandments.)
What are the first three about? (Loving God.)
practice: Give each child two pieces of gray paper, cut in a tablet shape (rounded top).
Write the numbers 1, 2 and 3 on the first tablet and 4 to 10 on the second.
Say the first three commandments slowly, in short child-friendly words: “God is first.” “Say God’s name with love.” “Keep Sunday holy.”
Let each child say them out loud, with the tablet in their hands.
script.close: Pray: “God, help us follow your commandments.” Sign of the Cross. Send home: “Tell your family the first three commandments.”

tryit: Make a pair of stone tablets.
lessons.saintStory:
Moses was born in Egypt when the Hebrew people were slaves. The king, called Pharaoh, was afraid of them, and a baby boy was in danger. Moses’ mother hid him in a basket on the river, where Pharaoh’s daughter found him and raised him as her own.
When he grew up, Moses had to run away to the desert, and there he became a shepherd. One day God spoke to him from a bush that burned but did not burn up. God said, “I have seen the suffering of my people. I am sending you to free them.” Moses was shy and said he could not talk well, but God said, “I will be with you.” With God’s help he led the people out of Egypt.
At Mount Sinai God gave him the Ten Commandments. Moses shows us that God can use a shy person, and that his rules are a gift for living well.

lessons.title: Jesus is God’s Son
lessons.idea: God sent his Son, Jesus, to save us. Jesus is God and man. He lived with Mary and Joseph in Nazareth.
lessons.question: What did Jesus do when he was a child?
lessons.activity: Draw the Holy Family at home in Nazareth and tell what each person does.
teach: Jesus is God’s Son who became man (CCC 422, 456). He lived in Nazareth, obeyed Mary and Joseph, and worked and prayed (CCC 531).
Luke 2:41–52 shows Jesus at twelve in the Temple.
Honor all kinds of families at home.
talk: What did Jesus do as a child?
Who helped him grow?
How do you help your family?
quiz: Jesus grew up in…|Nazareth|Egypt|Rome|Bethlehem|0|Luke 2:51.
Jesus is…|God’s Son|An angel|A king only|A prophet only|0|CCC 422.
Joseph was…|Jesus’s foster father|A shepherd|A priest|A king|0|Matthew 1.
lessons.life: Do one chore this week as Jesus would, cheerfully.
lessons.saint: Joseph: the quiet carpenter who protected Jesus and Mary.
misc: “Jesus was only pretending to be human.”
“Joseph is Jesus’ father in the same way as God.”
lessons.mem: Jesus, Mary and Joseph, be with us.
lessons.hook: Show a picture of the Holy Family. “Jesus had a family.”
lessons.assess: Ask: “Who lived with Jesus in Nazareth?”

script.open: Show a photograph of your own family, or a family picture from a book. Say, “This is my family. Look at what we do together at home. Today we will see what the family of Jesus was like.”
teach: Say: “Jesus is God’s Son. He is true God, and he is also a real boy who grew up. He had a mother, Mary, and a foster father, Joseph. They lived in a small town called Nazareth. We call them the Holy Family.”

Say: “Joseph was a carpenter. He worked with wood, and Jesus helped him. Mary cooked, cleaned and looked after them. Jesus obeyed them, and he grew bigger and wiser. What was his house like? It was probably small, and they were probably poor, but full of love.”

Tell the story from Luke 2:41-52: “When Jesus was twelve, he went to Jerusalem with Mary and Joseph for a feast. On the way home, they could not find him! They looked and looked. Three days later they found him in the Temple, talking with the teachers. Jesus said, ‘Did you not know that I must be in my Father’s house?’ Then he went home with them and obeyed them.”
ask: Who were Jesus’ mother and foster father? (Mary and Joseph.)
What did Joseph do for work? (He was a carpenter.)
How did Jesus treat his parents? (He obeyed them.)
practice: Give each child paper and crayons.
Say: “Draw the Holy Family at home in Nazareth. What is Joseph doing? What is Mary doing? What is Jesus doing?”
Walk around and ask each child to tell you about the picture.
Hang the pictures up. Say: “Our families are like the Holy Family, trying to love each other.”
script.close: Say the prayer together: “Jesus, Mary and Joseph, be with us.” Sign of the Cross. Send home: “Pray for your family tonight.”

tryit: Draw Jesus, Mary and Joseph at home.
Show what each one is doing.
lessons.saintStory:
Joseph was a carpenter in the town of Nazareth. The Bible calls him a “just” man, which means a good, faithful man who did what was right. He was engaged to Mary when the angel told him in a dream that Mary’s child was from the Holy Spirit and that he should not be afraid.
Joseph took Mary into his home and took care of her and the child. When King Herod wanted to harm baby Jesus, an angel warned Joseph in a dream. He got up in the night and took Mary and Jesus to Egypt, where they were safe. Later he brought them home to Nazareth, where he taught Jesus how to work with wood.
Joseph never says a word in the Gospels, but he always does what God asks. He shows what a good father is like, and we ask him to protect our families.

lessons.title: Jesus teaches and heals
lessons.idea: Jesus taught people about God’s love and healed the sick. He chose twelve friends, the apostles, to follow him.
lessons.question: Who were Jesus’ first friends?
lessons.activity: Act out the healing of the paralytic with a classmate lowered on a blanket (carefully).
teach: Jesus taught about God’s love and healed the sick (Mark 2:1–12; CCC 542, 547). He chose twelve apostles (CCC 551).
Apostle means “one who is sent.” Name Peter, Andrew, James and John.
Healing shows that Jesus cares for body and soul.
talk: Who did Jesus call first?
How did the friends help the man on the mat?
How can you be a good friend?
quiz: Jesus chose…|One apostle|None|Twelve apostles|Fifty apostles|2|Mark 3:14.
The friends lowered the man through…|The window|A tunnel|The door|The roof|3|Mark 2:4.
Jesus forgave the man’s…|Games|Homework|Debts|Sins|3|Mark 2:5.
lessons.life: Do something kind for a friend who is sad.
lessons.saint: Andrew: the fisherman who brought his brother Peter and a boy with loaves to Jesus.
lessons.mem: Follow me. (Mark 1:17)
lessons.hook: Say, “Imagine your best friends came with you everywhere.” Introduce the apostles.
lessons.assess: Ask: “Who did Jesus choose to follow him?”

script.open: Hold up a very big blanket and ask, “Who can lift a friend on a blanket without dropping him?” Get four children to hold the corners and lift a stuffed animal. “Four friends once did exactly this, to bring someone to Jesus.”
teach: Say: “When Jesus grew up, he began to teach about God. He walked by the Sea of Galilee. He saw two brothers, Peter and Andrew, fishing with nets. He said, ‘Follow me, and I will make you fishers of people.’ They left their nets and followed him. That is how Jesus began to choose twelve special friends called the apostles.”

Tell Mark 2:1-12: “One day Jesus was teaching in a house. It was so crowded, you could not get in. Four men were carrying a friend who could not walk. They could not get through the crowd. So they climbed up on the roof, made a hole, and lowered their friend down on his mat, right in front of Jesus! Jesus saw how much they trusted him. He said to the man, ‘Your sins are forgiven, get up and walk.’ And the man stood up, picked up his mat, and went home!”
Say: “Jesus teaches us about God’s love, and he helps people who are sick and sad. He still wants to help us today. And he asks us to follow him.”
ask: Who did Jesus choose to be his friends? (The twelve apostles. Peter and Andrew were fishermen.)
What did the four friends do to bring the man to Jesus? (They lowered him through the roof.)
How do you think the man felt? (Happy, amazed, thankful.)
practice: Choose four children to be the friends, one to be the man on the mat (a blanket), one to be Jesus.
Narrate the story while the children carefully lower the “man” (a child sitting on a blanket on the floor, or a stuffed animal).
Jesus says: “Get up and walk.” The man stands up and everyone cheers.
Switch roles so that more children can act it out.
script.close: Say: “Jesus, I want to follow you.” Sign of the Cross. Send home: “Who could you bring to Jesus this week? Invite a friend to pray with you.”

tryit: Listen to the story of the friends who lowered their friend through the roof.
Act it out with a blanket and a puppet.
lessons.saintStory:
Andrew was a fisherman on the Sea of Galilee. He first followed John the Baptist, and then one day John pointed to Jesus and said, “Behold, the Lamb of God!” Andrew went to find out, and he stayed with Jesus all day.
He was so happy that the first thing he did was run to tell his brother Simon, “We have found the Messiah!” and he brought Simon to Jesus. Jesus called Simon “Peter.” Later, when a crowd of thousands was hungry, it was Andrew who found a boy with five loaves and two fish and brought him to Jesus.
Andrew is known for bringing people to Jesus. Tradition says that he preached in many lands and died on an X-shaped cross. He shows us how to be good friends of Jesus, and to bring others to him.

lessons.title: Jesus dies and rises
lessons.idea: Jesus died on the cross to save us from sin. On the third day he rose from the dead. This is why we celebrate Easter.
lessons.question: What happened on Easter morning?
lessons.activity: Make an empty-tomb scene with a stone and a cloth. Sing “Alleluia.”
teach: Jesus died on the cross because he loves us, and rose on the third day (CCC 571, 638, 654). Keep Good Friday gentle.
Easter is the greatest feast: Jesus is alive.
Use simple language; avoid graphic details.
talk: What did the women find on Easter morning?
Why is Easter the happiest day?
How can we share Easter joy?
quiz: Jesus died to…|Hide|Be famous|Scare us|Save us|3|CCC 571.
On the third day Jesus…|Traveled|Stayed dead|Rose|Slept|2|Luke 24.
At Easter we sing…|Happy Birthday|Nothing|Silent Night|Alleluia|3|Liturgy.
lessons.life: Say “Alleluia!” whenever you hear a bell this Easter season.
lessons.saint: John the Apostle: the friend who stayed at the cross and ran to the empty tomb.
lessons.mem: He is risen! (Luke 24:6)
lessons.hook: Show a seed in dark soil. “It looks dead, but it grows.”
lessons.assess: Ask: “What happened on Easter morning?”

script.open: Say, “Now we come to the most important story of all, the center of our faith. Close your eyes, and listen.” Say it softly and slowly as if you were telling a secret.
teach: Tell: “Jesus was arrested, even though he had done nothing wrong. Soldiers made fun of him. They put a crown of thorns on his head. Then they nailed him to a cross. Jesus died. It was the saddest day. His mother Mary and his friends were there, and they cried. Jesus did this because he loves us. He took our sins on himself, so that we can be forgiven.”
Say: “They took his body down and laid it in a tomb, a cave in a rock, and rolled a big stone in front. It was dark and quiet. His friends were sad and scared.”

Tell with joy: “On the third day, very early, some women went to the tomb. The stone was rolled away. An angel said, ‘Do not be afraid. Jesus is not here. He is risen!’ Jesus was alive! He had risen from the dead. That is why we celebrate Easter, and why we say ‘Alleluia!’ Jesus died to save us, and Jesus rose to give us new life.”
ask: Why did Jesus die on the cross? (To save us from sin, because he loves us.)
What happened on the third day? (Jesus rose.)
What do we say at Easter? (Alleluia! He is risen!)
practice: Give each child a paper plate (for the stone), a brown paper tomb (a folded paper with an opening), and a small piece of white cloth.
Have the child put the cloth in the tomb and the “stone” in front.
Say: “It is Easter morning. Roll the stone away!” Children move the plate aside and see the empty tomb with the cloth.
Sing “Alleluia” together, clapping. Say, “He is risen!” and let children answer, “He is risen indeed!”
script.close: Pray: “Jesus, thank you for dying and rising for us.” Sign of the Cross. Send home: “Tell your family: Jesus is alive!”

lessons.saintStory:
John was a young fisherman who became one of Jesus’ twelve apostles. He was very close to Jesus, and at the Last Supper he leaned against Jesus’ chest.
When Jesus was arrested, most of the apostles ran away. John stayed. He stood at the foot of the cross with Mary, and Jesus said to him, “Behold your mother.” From that day John took Mary into his home. On Easter morning, when Mary Magdalene told them that the tomb was empty, John ran to it. He got there first, and he saw the cloths lying there and believed.
John lived to be an old man, and he wrote the Gospel of John. He shows us how to stay near Jesus, even in the hardest moments, and how happy it is to find him alive.

units.title: The Holy Spirit and the Church

lessons.title: The Holy Spirit is our helper
lessons.idea: Jesus sent the Holy Spirit to help us. The Spirit came on Pentecost as wind and fire.
lessons.question: What does the Holy Spirit help us do?
lessons.activity: Make paper flames and a red mobile. Pray, “Come, Holy Spirit.”
teach: Jesus promised to send the Holy Spirit (John 14:16). At Pentecost, wind and fire came (Acts 2:1–4; CCC 731–732).
The Spirit helps us to love, be brave and pray.
The Spirit is God, not a ghost.
talk: What did the apostles see and hear?
How does the Holy Spirit help us?
When do you need help?
quiz: The Holy Spirit came as…|Wind and fire|A bird only|A rainbow|Rain|0|Acts 2:2-3.
The Holy Spirit is…|A saint|God|A ghost|An angel|1|CCC 685.
Pentecost is the Church’s…|Holiday|Funeral|Birthday|Test|2|CCC 726.
lessons.life: Ask the Holy Spirit for help before something that feels hard.
lessons.saint: Philip Neri: a joyful priest who felt the Holy Spirit like fire in his heart.
lessons.mem: Come, Holy Spirit.
lessons.hook: Blow on a pinwheel. “You can’t see wind, but you can see what it does.”
lessons.assess: Ask: “What came on Pentecost? What does the Spirit do?”

script.open: Take the class to the window, or use a handheld fan. Ask the children to put their hand in front of the fan. “Can you see the wind? No! But can you feel it? Yes. The wind is real, even if you cannot see it. Today we meet someone who is real, but we cannot see.”
teach: Say: “Jesus was going back to heaven. He told his friends, ‘I will not leave you alone. I will send the Holy Spirit, who will be your helper.’ The Holy Spirit is God, just like the Father and the Son.”

Tell Acts 2: “The friends of Jesus were gathered in a room, praying. All of a sudden they heard a sound like a mighty wind. And something that looked like flames of fire rested on each one of them. The Holy Spirit came! They were filled with courage and joy, and they went out and told everyone about Jesus. This was Pentecost, the birthday of the Church.”
Say: “The Holy Spirit is our helper too. He came to you at Baptism. He helps us pray, be brave, know right from wrong, and love other people. We can say: ‘Come, Holy Spirit,’ any time we need help.”
ask: Who did Jesus send to help us? (The Holy Spirit.)
What did the Spirit look like at Pentecost? (Wind and fire.)
When can we ask the Holy Spirit for help? (Always: before school, when we are scared, when we have a choice.)
practice: Cut flame shapes out of red, orange and yellow paper.
Give each child three flames, and let them write or draw “Come, Holy Spirit” on one.
Hang the flames from a red paper circle or paper plate with yarn, to make a mobile.
While hanging, pray together, “Come, Holy Spirit.” Blow gently so that the flames move like in a wind.
script.close: Pray: “Come, Holy Spirit, fill our hearts.” Sign of the Cross. Send home: “Say ‘Come, Holy Spirit’ before you do something hard.”

tryit: Hang them on a red mobile.
lessons.saintStory:
Philip Neri was born in Florence, Italy, in 1515. As a young man he went to Rome, where he did not want to be rich. He wanted to help people and pray.
He cared for the poor and sick, and he gathered young people around him to talk, to pray and to sing. He was a very funny man who loved a good joke, and he said that a joyful heart is a gift of the Holy Spirit. Once, on the night before Pentecost in 1544, he was praying, and he felt a joyful fire of love in his heart.
Philip lived joyfully for many years, and people loved him. He reminds us that the Holy Spirit gives us happiness and love, and helps us be good friends.

lessons.title: The Church is God’s family
lessons.idea: The Church is God’s family. The Pope and bishops lead her. All baptized people belong to Jesus’ family.
lessons.question: Who leads the Church?
lessons.activity: Show pictures of the Pope, our bishop and our pastor. Match each to their job.
teach: The Church is God’s family (CCC 751, 771). Jesus gave Peter authority; the Pope is Peter’s successor (CCC 881).
The bishop leads a diocese; the pastor leads the parish.
Use names and pictures of your bishop and pastor.
talk: Who is the pastor of your parish?
What does the bishop do?
Why do we pray for the Pope?
quiz: The Pope leads…|The whole Church|A band|One town|One school|0|CCC 882.
A bishop leads a…|Diocese|Store|City council|Team|0|CCC 886.
Priests serve in…|Schools only|Zoos|Banks|Parishes|3|CCC 1562.
lessons.life: Pray for the Pope, your bishop and your pastor by name.
lessons.saint: Peter: the first Pope.
lessons.mem: We are the Church.
lessons.hook: Hold a family photo. “The Church is a big family.”
lessons.assess: Ask: “Who leads the Church? Who leads our parish?”

script.open: Hold up a framed family photo. Ask, “Who is the head of this family?” Take answers. “Now think of a big family, bigger than any town. It is God’s family, called the Church.”
teach: Say: “Who belongs to God’s family? Everyone who is baptized. Boys and girls, mothers and fathers, grandmas and grandpas, from all over the world. That is the Church.”

Say: “Every family needs people to lead and take care of it. Jesus chose Peter to be the leader of his friends. He said, ‘You are Peter, and on this rock I will build my Church.’ Peter was the first pope. The Pope today is a successor of Peter. He is the leader of the whole Church, and we pray for him.”

Say: “The Pope has helpers. They are bishops, who lead the Church in each area, and priests, who help at the parish. Also deacons, sisters, and the people who teach you. And you! Each baptized person is part of the family. We all have a job: to love Jesus and each other.”
ask: Who is the leader of the whole Church? (The Pope.)
Who is the leader of our diocese? (Our bishop.) Of our parish? (Our priest, Father ___.)
Who is in God’s family? (All the baptized, including you!)
practice: Show three photos: the Pope, your bishop, your pastor.
Set out three labels: “Leads the whole Church,” “Leads our diocese,” “Leads our parish.” Ask children to match each photo to its label.
Say each name aloud together and wave: “Hello, Pope ___, Bishop ___, Father ___.”
Pray: “Lord, bless the Pope, our bishop, and our priest.”
script.close: Say: “We are the Church.” Sign of the Cross. Send home: “Pray for the Pope this week.”

tryit: Look at pictures of the Pope, our bishop and our priest.
Match each one to their job.
lessons.saintStory:
Simon was a fisherman by the Sea of Galilee when Jesus called him. Jesus gave him a new name, Peter, which means “rock.” Jesus said, “You are Peter, and on this rock I will build my Church.”
Peter was not perfect. He often spoke before thinking. On the night before Jesus died, he was afraid and said three times that he did not know him. But after Jesus rose, he asked Peter three times, “Do you love me?” and Peter said, “Yes, Lord, you know that I love you.” Jesus told him, “Feed my sheep.”
Peter led the first Christians and later went to Rome. He is the first Pope, and every pope after him has led the Church. He shows us that Jesus forgives and still gives us work to do.

lessons.title: The Trinity
lessons.idea: There is one God in three Persons: Father, Son and Holy Spirit. We say it when we make the Sign of the Cross.
lessons.question: What do we say in the Sign of the Cross?
lessons.activity: Show a shamrock or a three-part drawing. Practice the Sign of the Cross.
teach: There is one God in three Persons: Father, Son, Holy Spirit (CCC 232, 253). It is a mystery.
We say it in the Sign of the Cross and Glory Be.
Do not force analogies; a shamrock is only a help.
talk: Who do we pray to in the Sign of the Cross?
How many Gods are there?
What do the Father, Son and Spirit each do?
quiz: How many Gods are there?|Three|Two|One|Many|2|CCC 253.
The three Persons are…|Father, Son and Holy Spirit|Three angels|Mom, Dad and me|Peter, Paul, Mary|0|CCC 253.
We begin prayer with…|A clap|A shout|The Sign of the Cross|Nothing|2|CCC 2157.
lessons.life: Make the Sign of the Cross slowly each time you pray.
lessons.saint: Patrick: he taught the Irish about the Trinity.
misc: “God is just one person with three names.”
lessons.mem: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.
lessons.hook: Trace the Sign of the Cross slowly. “We name three Persons.”
lessons.assess: Ask children to make the Sign of the Cross and name the three Persons.

script.open: Hold up a three-leaf clover or a drawing of one. Say, “This is a shamrock. How many leaves? Three. But is it three plants or one plant? One. It is one plant, with three leaves.” Pause. “This will help us with something very hard to understand.”
teach: Say: “There is only one God. And in that one God, there are three Persons: the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. Not three gods. One God. We call this the Trinity. The word Trinity means ‘three in one.’”

Say: “It is a mystery, which means something so great that we cannot completely understand it. But we can know it is true, because Jesus told us. When Jesus was baptized, the Father’s voice spoke from heaven, the Son stood in the water, and the Holy Spirit came down like a dove. All three were there!”

Say: “Every time we make the Sign of the Cross, we say the name of the Trinity: ‘In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit.’ And we pray, ‘Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.’ When you pray, you are talking to God, who is Father, Son and Holy Spirit.”
ask: How many gods are there? (One.) How many Persons? (Three.)
What are their names? (Father, Son, Holy Spirit.)
When do we say the Trinity’s names? (When we make the Sign of the Cross.)
practice: Draw a shamrock on the board with three leaves, and label the leaves Father, Son, Holy Spirit.
Give each child a green paper shamrock to color and label.
Practice the Sign of the Cross slowly, saying each name, five times.
Say the Glory Be together.
script.close: Say the Glory Be. Sign of the Cross. Send home: “Make the Sign of the Cross slowly and say the names of the Trinity.”

tryit: Practice the Sign of the Cross.
lessons.saintStory:
Patrick was born around the year 385 in Britain. When he was sixteen, pirates kidnapped him and took him to Ireland, where he had to work as a shepherd. He was lonely and afraid, so he prayed, many times each day.
After six years Patrick escaped and went home. But he had a dream in which the people of Ireland called him to come back. He studied to be a priest and became a bishop, and he returned to Ireland. He taught people about God for many years and baptized many of them.
It is said that Patrick used a shamrock, a plant with three leaves on one stem, to teach about the Trinity: one God in three Persons. Patrick helps us see that God is one, and is also Father, Son and Holy Spirit.

lessons.title: Mary, our mother
lessons.idea: Mary is the mother of Jesus. She is also our mother. She said yes to God and helps us say yes too.
lessons.question: What did Mary say to the angel?
lessons.activity: Learn the Hail Mary. Make a small flower garland for Mary.
teach: Mary is Jesus’ mother and our mother (Luke 1:26–38; John 19:25–27; CCC 495, 501, 963).
Mary said yes to God. Teach the first half of the Hail Mary.
Mary always leads us to Jesus.
talk: What did the angel say to Mary?
Why do we ask Mary to pray for us?
How can you say yes to God?
quiz: Mary is…|Jesus’s mother|A neighbor|A queen of the sea|A teacher|0|Luke 1.
The Hail Mary begins with the words of…|The angel|Joseph|The Pope|A shepherd|0|Luke 1:28.
Mary is our…|Boss|Servant|Stranger|Mother too|3|John 19:27.
lessons.life: Say a Hail Mary each day this week.
lessons.saint: Maximilian Kolbe: a priest who loved Mary and gave his life to save another man.
lessons.mem: Hail Mary, full of grace, the Lord is with thee.
lessons.hook: Hold a flower. “We give flowers to people we love. We give them to Mary.”
lessons.assess: Ask: “What did Mary say to the angel?”

script.open: Bring a bunch of flowers and a picture of Mary. Say, “When we love someone, we bring them flowers. Who do you think these flowers are for? For our mother in heaven. Let’s learn to talk to her.”
teach: Say: “When Jesus was dying on the cross, he looked at his friend John, and at his mother Mary, and said to John, ‘Here is your mother.’ Jesus gave Mary to all of us. She is our mother too.”
Say: “Mary said yes to God when the angel Gabriel came. She said, ‘Let it be done to me according to your word.’ She helps us say yes to God, too. And she always leads us to Jesus.”

Teach the Hail Mary in two parts: “First, the words of the angel and Elizabeth: ‘Hail Mary, full of grace, the Lord is with thee. Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb, Jesus.’ Second, we ask her to pray: ‘Holy Mary, Mother of God, pray for us sinners, now and at the hour of our death. Amen.’”
ask: Who is Mary? (Jesus’ mother. And our mother too.)
What did Mary say to God? (Yes.)
What do we ask Mary to do in the Hail Mary? (Pray for us.)
practice: Say the Hail Mary line by line, children repeating each line, three times.
Give each child paper flowers and a length of yarn. Help them tape or tie the flowers to make a garland.
While working, whisper the Hail Mary together.
Place the garland around a picture or statue of Mary, praying the Hail Mary one more time.
script.close: Pray one Hail Mary. Sign of the Cross. Send home: “Say a Hail Mary with someone at home tonight.”

lessons.saintStory:
Raymond Kolbe was born in Poland in 1894. When he was a boy, he said Mary appeared to him and offered him two crowns, a white one for purity and a red one for martyrdom, and he said yes to both. He became a Franciscan priest and took the name Maximilian.
Father Kolbe loved Mary very much. He started a magazine and a city of friars, to teach people about her. When the Nazis invaded Poland in World War II, they put him in the prison camp at Auschwitz. In 1941, when a man was chosen to die and cried for his family, Maximilian said, “I will take his place.” He died in the man’s place.
Maximilian shows us that Mary leads us to Jesus, and that love is willing to give everything.

lessons.title: Saints are our friends
lessons.idea: Saints followed Jesus well. They are in heaven and pray for us. We learn from their lives.
lessons.question: Which saint would you like to meet?
lessons.activity: Read a short story of a saint (Francis, Thérèse, or Patrick). Draw a favorite scene.
teach: Saints are in heaven and pray for us (CCC 828, 957). Hebrews 12:1 calls them witnesses.
Tell one saint’s story (Francis, Thérèse, Patrick).
Saints were children, too, like Maria Goretti or Carlo Acutis.
talk: What did the saint do?
What can we learn from them?
Whom would you like to meet?
quiz: Saints are…|Make-believe|Only popes|With God in heaven|Cartoon characters|2|CCC 828.
Saints pray for…|Only the poor|Us|Nobody|Only angels|1|CCC 956.
Many saints were…|Kings only|Soldiers only|Ordinary people who loved God|Rich only|2|CCC 2030.
lessons.life: Draw your favorite saint and put it on the fridge.
lessons.saint: Kateri Tekakwitha: a young Native American woman who loved Jesus and was faithful.
lessons.mem: Holy Saint, pray for us.
lessons.hook: Show a picture of a saint. “Saints are people who loved Jesus.”
lessons.assess: Ask: “What did your saint do to love God?”

script.open: Put several framed pictures of saints (or a book of saints) on a table. Say, “Who are these people? They are not movie stars or sports heroes. They are heroes of a different kind. They are our friends in heaven.”
teach: Say: “The Bible tells us that we are surrounded by a great cloud of witnesses (Hebrews 12:1). That means that many people who have already died are cheering for us from heaven. We call them saints.”

Say: “Saints are not perfect people. They are people who tried very hard to follow Jesus, and they asked him for help when they failed. Some were poor, some were rich, some were kids like you. Some were brave, some were shy. They all loved God.”

Say: “The saints are alive in heaven. They are close to God. When we ask, ‘Saint Francis, pray for us,’ they pray for us, as a friend would. They also show us how to live. Reading about saints is like reading a story that is true.”
ask: What is a saint? (A person who followed Jesus and is in heaven.)
What do saints do for us? (Pray for us and show us how to live.)
Who is your favorite saint? (Take answers.)
practice: Tell the story of Kateri, or of Francis, or of Thérèse, in your own words, with a picture book if possible.
Give each child paper and crayons.
Say: “Draw your favorite part of the story.”
Let children show and tell, then say together: “Saint ___, pray for us.”
script.close: Say the Guardian Angel prayer or: “All holy men and women, pray for us.” Sign of the Cross. Send home: “Ask your family which saint they love.”

tryit: Listen to the story of a saint.
lessons.saintStory:
Kateri was born in 1656 in a Mohawk village in what is now New York. When she was four, smallpox took her parents and her little brother, and left her face scarred and her eyesight weak. An uncle raised her.
When a Jesuit priest, a “Blackrobe,” came to the village, Kateri listened to him and learned about Jesus. She was baptized at twenty, on Easter Sunday in 1676. Her family and others did not like it, and she was treated badly. To keep her faith, she walked about two hundred miles to a mission village in Canada.
There she prayed, cared for the sick and old, and lived a quiet, holy life. She died at twenty-four, and her friends said her face became beautiful in death. She was named a saint in 2012. Kateri shows that saints come from every people, and that they stay faithful to Jesus even in hard times.

lessons.title: Our guardian angels
lessons.idea: God gives each of us a guardian angel. Angels praise God and help us on our way to heaven.
lessons.question: How does your angel help you?
lessons.activity: Practice the Guardian Angel prayer. Draw an angel beside your bed.
teach: Each person has a guardian angel (CCC 332, 336; Psalm 91:11). Angels are pure spirits who serve God.
Pray the Guardian Angel prayer each night.
Angels have no bodies; pictures are only signs.
talk: How do you think your angel helps?
When do you feel safe?
What would you say to your angel?
quiz: Angels are…|Stars|Statues|Spirits who serve God|Ghosts|2|CCC 328.
We each have…|No angel|A pet angel|Two angels|A guardian angel|3|CCC 336.
Angels praise…|The moon|God|Us|The sun|1|Psalm 148:2.
lessons.life: Thank your guardian angel every night.
lessons.saint: Archangel Michael: defends God’s people.
lessons.mem: Angel of God, my guardian dear, to whom God’s love commits me here, ever this day be at my side, to light and guard, to rule and guide. Amen.
lessons.hook: Say, “Someone is watching over you right now!” Show an angel picture.
lessons.assess: Ask children to say the prayer with you.

script.open: Bring a small stuffed animal to guard something, or tell the children, “Close your eyes. I’m going to put something under this cloth. One of you will protect it.” Place a small object, and choose a child as the “guard” to stand next to it. “A guard keeps watch. God gives each of us a guard of our own, and it is a very special kind.”
teach: Say: “Angels are real. They are not people who died. God made them before the world began. They have no bodies, but they are alive. They are very strong and very smart, and they love and praise God all the time. Their name means ‘messenger,’ because God sends them with messages.”

Say: “Do you remember some angels in the Bible? Gabriel told Mary she would be Jesus’ mother. Angels sang to the shepherds at Christmas. An angel told Joseph to take Jesus to Egypt. Angels helped Jesus in the desert.”

Say: “God has given each of us a guardian angel who stays with us all our life. He guards us, helps us do good and leads us to heaven. Psalm 91 says: ‘He will give his angels charge over you, to guard you in all your ways.’ You never walk alone.”
ask: What are angels? (God’s helpers and messengers.)
Who gave us a guardian angel? (God.)
When can we pray to our guardian angel? (Any time: morning, scary times, bedtime.)
practice: Teach the Guardian Angel prayer line by line.
Say it three times together.
Give each child paper. Say: “Draw your bed and your guardian angel standing beside it.”
While they draw, whisper the prayer together once more.
script.close: Say the Guardian Angel prayer together. Sign of the Cross. Send home: “Say the Guardian Angel prayer every night this week.”

tryit: Draw an angel beside a bed.
lessons.saintStory:
The name Michael means “Who is like God?” He is an archangel, one of the great angels who serve God. The Bible, in the book of Revelation, tells of a battle in heaven where Michael and his angels fought against the dragon, Satan, and won.
Michael is the protector of God’s people. In the Book of Daniel he is called “the great prince who protects your people.” For many centuries Christians have prayed to him for protection from evil. Soldiers, police and rescue workers pray to him for help.
We often see Michael in pictures with a sword, standing over the dragon. He reminds us that God is stronger than evil, and that God’s angels help us.

units.title: The sacraments
units.eq: How does Jesus stay with us?

lessons.title: Baptism
lessons.idea: In Baptism we are washed with water and receive the Holy Spirit. We become children of God and members of the Church.
lessons.question: What things do we see at a baptism?
lessons.activity: Handle a baptismal candle and shell. Retell the baptism of Jesus.
teach: Baptism makes us God’s children and members of the Church (CCC 1213, 1239, 1262). Show the water, oil, white garment and candle.
Jesus was baptized by John (Matthew 3:13–17).
Ask families to share baptism photos.
talk: What happens at a baptism?
Who are your godparents?
What does the candle mean?
quiz: Baptism uses…|Fire|Wind|Sand|Water|3|CCC 1214.
The baptismal candle shows…|A birthday|Nothing|Christ the light|A game|2|CCC 1243.
Baptism makes us…|Teachers|Kings|Angels|Children of God|3|CCC 1265.
lessons.life: Light a candle at home on your baptism day each year.
lessons.saint: John the Baptist: baptized Jesus in the Jordan.
lessons.mem: I am a child of God.
lessons.hook: Pour water over a doll’s hand. “Water makes us clean and gives life.”
lessons.assess: Ask: “What happens in Baptism?”

script.open: Bring a small bowl of water and a shell. Say, “What can water do? It can make things clean. It can give things life, like plants. Today we will find out about the water that does something even more special.”
teach: Tell Matthew 3:13-17: “One day Jesus went to the Jordan River, where John was baptizing people. John said, ‘I should be baptized by you.’ But Jesus said, ‘Let it be so now.’ John baptized him. When Jesus came up out of the water, the heavens opened. The Holy Spirit came down like a dove. And a voice from heaven said, ‘This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased.’ All three Persons of the Trinity were there.”

Say: “Today, when a person is baptized, the priest pours water on their head, or puts them in the water, and says, ‘I baptize you in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit.’ Something wonderful happens. Sin is washed away. The Holy Spirit comes to live in us. We become children of God and members of the Church.”

Say: “At Baptism, we receive a white garment and a lighted candle. The white garment means we are new and clean. The candle means Christ is our light. And God says to each of us what he said to Jesus: ‘You are my beloved child.’”
ask: Who baptized Jesus? (John the Baptist.)
What words are said at Baptism? (In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit.)
What happens to us at Baptism? (We become God’s children and part of the Church.)
practice: Show the baptismal candle, shell and white cloth.
Choose one child to be Jesus and one to be John. Others are the crowd. Use a small bowl of water.
Retell the story. John pours a little water over Jesus’s hand; the “heavens” open (children raise arms) and everyone says, “This is my beloved Son!”
Let each child touch the water and say, “I am a child of God.”
script.close: Make the Sign of the Cross with water, touching each child’s forehead if you can, or each child touching their own. Send home: “Ask your parents about your baptism day.”

tryit: Look at a baptismal candle and a shell.
Act out the baptism of Jesus.
Say: “I am a child of God.”
lessons.saintStory:
John the Baptist was a cousin of Jesus, born to Zechariah and Elizabeth when they were old. An angel had told Zechariah that his son would prepare the way for the Lord.
When John grew up, he lived in the desert and wore a rough coat of camel’s hair. People came from far to hear him. He told them to turn away from their sins, and he baptized them in the Jordan River as a sign of a new start.
One day Jesus came to John to be baptized. John said, “I should be baptized by you!” But Jesus asked him, and John baptized him. The heavens opened, the Spirit came down like a dove, and a voice said, “This is my beloved Son.” John the Baptist shows us how Baptism opens the door to God’s family.

lessons.title: The Mass
lessons.idea: At Mass we listen to God’s word and share in Jesus’ sacrifice. We receive Jesus in Holy Communion.
lessons.question: What are the two main parts of the Mass?
lessons.activity: Match pictures of the parts of Mass in order.
teach: At Mass we listen to God’s word and share in Jesus’ sacrifice (CCC 1346, 1348). Walk through the order with pictures.
Emmaus (Luke 24:13–35): Jesus is known in the breaking of bread.
Practice responses: “And with your spirit.”
talk: What do we hear at Mass?
Who do we receive in Communion?
What do you like best about Mass?
quiz: Mass has…|No parts|Two main parts|Ten parts|One part|1|CCC 1346.
In Communion we receive…|A coin|Jesus|A picture|Bread only|1|CCC 1374.
We listen to…|God’s word|Music only|Gossip|The weather|0|CCC 1349.
lessons.life: At Mass this week, listen for one word from the Gospel and tell someone after.
lessons.saint: Justin Martyr: a teacher who wrote down what Christians do at Mass, about 1,800 years ago.
lessons.mem: Lord, I am not worthy that you should enter under my roof, but only say the word and my soul shall be healed.
lessons.hook: Set out cards of the Mass in a row. “What do you see at Mass?”
lessons.assess: Ask children to put four Mass cards in order.

script.open: Show the children a loaf of bread, and ask, “What happens at Mass? What do we do?” Let them name things. “We are going to put the parts of Mass in order, like pieces of a puzzle.”
teach: Say: “Mass is the greatest prayer of the Church. At Mass, Jesus is with us in a special way. The Mass has two big parts. In the first part, we listen to God’s word. In the second part, we share in Jesus’ gift, the Eucharist.”

Tell Luke 24:13-35 briefly: “After Jesus rose, two friends were walking to a town called Emmaus. They were sad. A stranger joined them, and he explained the Scriptures to them. When they got to the village, they asked him to stay for dinner. He took bread, blessed it, broke it and gave it to them. And suddenly they recognized him. It was Jesus! Then he disappeared. They said, ‘Did not our hearts burn within us while he spoke?’”

Say: “The Mass is just like this. First we listen to the readings, and the priest explains. Then the priest takes bread and wine and says Jesus’ words, and they become Jesus’ Body and Blood. We receive Jesus in Communion. And then we are sent out to tell people about him.”
ask: What are the two big parts of Mass? (Listening to God’s word, and the Eucharist.)
Who is with us at Mass? (Jesus.)
How did the two friends know it was Jesus? (When he broke the bread.)
practice: Prepare picture cards for the Mass: the entrance, the readings, the homily, the offering of bread and wine, Communion, and the blessing.
Mix the cards up, and have children put them in order.
For each, ask: “What do we do here?” and “What do we say?”
Practice the responses: “And with your spirit,” “Thanks be to God,” “Amen.”
script.close: Say the prayer together: “Lord, I am not worthy to receive you, but only say the word and I shall be healed.” Sign of the Cross. Send home: “At Mass, listen for the Gospel.”

tryit: Put the Mass pictures in order.
Tell what happens in each one.
lessons.saintStory:
Justin was born about the year 100 in a town in the land of Samaria. He loved to study and was always looking for the truth. He tried many kinds of teachers, then one day he met an old man by the sea who told him about Jesus. Justin became a Christian.
He traveled to Rome and opened a school. He wrote a letter to the emperor to explain what Christians believed and what they did on Sunday. He described the very same things we do at Mass: readings from the Bible, a talk, prayers, bread and wine brought forward, and the people saying “Amen.”
Justin was put to death for his faith around the year 165. He is called Justin Martyr. He shows us that the Mass is very old, and that Christians have gathered like this since the beginning.

lessons.title: Being sorry and forgiven
lessons.idea: When we sin we can say sorry. In Reconciliation the priest, in Jesus’ name, forgives us.
lessons.question: Who forgives our sins?
lessons.activity: Practice an examination of conscience with simple questions and an Act of Contrition.
teach: When we sin we can say sorry. God is happy when we return (Luke 15:1–10; CCC 1440–1441). In Reconciliation the priest forgives in Jesus’ name (CCC 1449).
Practice a gentle examination: Was I kind? Did I tell the truth?
Never shame.
talk: How does God feel when we say sorry?
Who helps us say sorry?
How do we feel after?
quiz: In Reconciliation, the priest…|Judges|Hides|Scolds|Forgives in Jesus’s name|3|CCC 1461.
God’s forgiveness is…|Lost|Always ready|Late|Rare|1|CCC 1443.
We tell the priest our…|Sins|Games|Dreams|Toys|0|CCC 1456.
lessons.life: Practice saying “I’m sorry, and I will try again.”
lessons.saint: John Vianney: he heard confessions for hours so people could meet God’s mercy.
misc: “God stops loving me when I sin.”
lessons.mem: O my God, I am sorry for my sins. Help me to do better. Amen.
lessons.hook: Tell the story of the lost sheep. “How does the shepherd feel when he finds it?”
lessons.assess: Ask: “What do we say when we are sorry?”

script.open: Spill a little bit of water on the floor and say, “Oops. I made a mess. What do I need to do?” Let them say to clean it up. “When we do something wrong, we make a kind of mess in our hearts. And God has a way to clean it up.”
teach: Tell Luke 15:1-10: “Jesus told a story about a shepherd with one hundred sheep. One got lost. What did the shepherd do? He left the other ninety-nine and went to find the lost one. When he found it, he put it on his shoulders and went home happy. And he said to his friends, ‘Come and celebrate with me.’ Jesus said that God is like that shepherd, and that there is joy in heaven over one person who says sorry.”

Say: “When we sin, we hurt God, other people and ourselves. But God is always ready to forgive. Jesus gave the Church a special sacrament so we can hear his forgiveness. It is called Reconciliation, or Confession. We tell our sins to the priest, he gives us advice, and then, in Jesus’ name, he says, ‘I absolve you from your sins.’”
Say: “It may feel scary. But it is a wonderful gift. We get to hear God say, ‘I forgive you.’ We start fresh. We feel light and happy again.”
ask: Who is the shepherd in the story? (Jesus, or God.)
What does God want to do when we are sorry? (Forgive us.)
What do we do first when we get ready for Confession? (Think about what we did wrong.)
practice: Teach the first steps for a child: 1. Say a short prayer. 2. Think about the day: Did I obey? Was I kind? Did I tell the truth? 3. Say what I did wrong. 4. Say the Act of Contrition.
Practice thinking through three questions with the group, quietly.
Say the Act of Contrition line by line: “O my God, I am sorry for my sins. Help me to do better. Amen.”
Close with a “Thank you, God, for forgiving us.”
script.close: Pray the Act of Contrition together. Sign of the Cross. Send home: “Ask when you can go to Confession as a family.”

tryit: Listen to the story of the lost sheep.
lessons.saintStory:
John Vianney was born in France in 1786. He was a farm boy who found it very hard to study, but he wanted to be a priest more than anything. After years of effort, he was ordained, and in 1818 he was sent to a tiny village called Ars.
The village was poor and hardly anyone went to church. Father Vianney visited the people, taught the children and prayed. Slowly, hearts changed. People began to come to him to confess their sins, so many that he spent up to sixteen hours a day in the confessional, and people traveled from far away to see him. He ate little and slept very little.
He is called the Curé of Ars, and is the patron of parish priests. He shows us that God’s mercy is great, and that a priest in Confession is a way for us to meet it.

units.title: Living as Jesus’ friends
units.eq: How do friends of Jesus live?

lessons.title: The Golden Rule
lessons.idea: Treat others as you want to be treated. This is how Jesus teaches us to love.
lessons.question: How do you want others to treat you?
lessons.activity: Role-play kind and unkind responses; practice the kind ones.
teach: The Golden Rule: treat others as you want to be treated (Matthew 7:12; CCC 1789, 2055).
Role-play kind words. Ask how each feels.
Link to forgiveness and sharing.
talk: How do you want to be treated?
What is a kind word?
How can you help someone who is left out?
quiz: The Golden Rule says…|Treat others as you want to be treated|Win|Hide|Be first|0|Matthew 7:12.
Jesus taught us to…|Fight|Hide|Love|Buy|2|John 13:34.
A kind act is…|Yelling|Taking|Sharing|Pushing|2|Luke 6:31.
lessons.life: Be the first to include a classmate who is alone.
lessons.saint: Elizabeth of Hungary: a queen who fed the poor.
lessons.mem: Do to others what you would have them do to you. (Matthew 7:12)
lessons.hook: Act out sharing a toy two ways. “Which way would you like?”
lessons.assess: Ask for an example of the Golden Rule.

script.open: Play “the unfair snack”: give one child a cookie and tell the others they cannot have any. Ask, “How did that feel? What if I did that to you?” Then say, “Jesus gave us a simple rule to help us in these moments.”
teach: Say: “Jesus said, ‘Do to others whatever you would have them do to you.’ (Matthew 7:12) We call this the Golden Rule. It is golden because it is so valuable. It means: before you do or say something, ask yourself, ‘How would I feel if someone did this to me?’”

Say: “If you would like someone to share, then you share. If you would like to be invited, then you invite someone. If you do not like being called names, do not call anyone names. If you want to be forgiven, forgive.”

Say: “This is how Jesus teaches us to love. Loving someone means thinking about what they need and feel. The Golden Rule works at home, at school, at the playground, with friends and with people we do not like very much.”
ask: What is the Golden Rule? (Treat others how you want to be treated.)
What would you want if you fell down at the playground? (Help, kindness.)
Who can you treat with the Golden Rule this week? (Take answers.)
practice: Give two cards to pairs: “Kind way” and “Unkind way.” Read a situation (someone is alone at recess, someone spills their lunch).
Let one child act out an unkind response, and then a kind one.
Talk about how each one feels.
Say the Golden Rule together, three times, with a motion: point to self, then to others.
script.close: Pray: “Jesus, help us treat others the way we want to be treated.” Sign of the Cross. Send home: “Do one kind thing and tell us about it.”

tryit: Act out kind and unkind ways to treat someone.
lessons.saintStory:
Elizabeth was born in 1207, the daughter of the king of Hungary. When she was fourteen she married a good young man named Louis, who ruled a part of Germany. They loved each other and loved God.
Elizabeth could have lived in a castle with all kinds of fine food and clothes, but she paid attention to the poor. She gave away food and money. She built a hospital and cared for the sick herself. Once, the story goes, she was carrying bread to the poor under her cloak and when someone asked what she had, it had turned into roses.
Elizabeth’s husband died when she was twenty. She gave up her riches to serve the poor, and she died at twenty-four. She shows us how to treat others as we want to be treated: with kindness.

lessons.title: Obey and honor
lessons.idea: We honor our parents and teachers. We follow rules that keep us safe and help us grow.
lessons.question: Who helps keep you safe?
lessons.activity: Make a thank-you card to a parent or teacher.
teach: Honor your father and mother (Exodus 20:12; CCC 2214, 2216). Obedience is listening because we trust.
Jesus obeyed Mary and Joseph (Luke 2:51).
Parents also have duties; praise respectful families.
talk: Who keeps you safe?
Why are rules good?
How do you honor your parents?
quiz: The fourth commandment says…|Rest|Don’t lie|Don’t steal|Honor your father and mother|3|Exodus 20:12.
Jesus obeyed…|Nobody|Strangers|Soldiers|Mary and Joseph|3|Luke 2:51.
Obeying helps us…|Grow|Hurt|Fight|Hide|0|CCC 2216.
lessons.life: Say “Yes, Mom/Dad” cheerfully this week.
lessons.saint: Dominic Savio: a boy saint who obeyed his teacher and did small things with great love.
lessons.mem: Honor your father and mother.
lessons.hook: Show thank-you cards. “Who takes care of you? How can you thank them?”
lessons.assess: Ask: “How can you honor your family?”

script.open: Say, “I need two volunteers: one to be a ‘parent’ and one to be a ‘child.’ The parent says, ‘Please put your shoes away.’ The child can do three things: ignore, argue or obey. Which is best, and why?” Let them act it out and talk about it.
teach: Say: “One of God’s commandments says, ‘Honor your father and your mother.’ This is the fourth commandment, and the first one with a promise: ‘so that you may live long.’ (Ephesians 6:1-3) To honor means to respect and love, and to listen.”

Say: “Our parents, teachers and others take care of us. They give us food, a home, help and love. They make rules to keep us safe and to help us grow. When we obey them, we show love, and we help our family be happy. Remember that Jesus obeyed Mary and Joseph.”

Say: “It is not always easy! Sometimes we want to do something else. But when we obey with a good heart, we are growing in goodness. We can also say thank you. A thank-you is a way of honoring someone.”
ask: Why do we obey our parents and teachers? (To honor them, and because they love and take care of us.)
How did Jesus treat Mary and Joseph? (He obeyed them.)
How can you say thank you to your parents? (Words, help, a card, a hug.)
practice: Give each child a folded piece of paper and crayons.
Say: “Decorate the front of your card. Inside, we will write why we are thankful.”
Help each child write “Thank you for ______” and sign their name.
Let them decorate with stickers or drawings, then take the cards home.
script.close: Pray: “God, bless our parents and teachers.” Sign of the Cross. Send home: “Give the card, and give a hug.”

tryit: Give it to your parent or teacher.
lessons.saintStory:
Dominic Savio was born in Italy in 1842 to a poor family. He was a quiet, cheerful boy who loved to pray. At seven he made his First Communion, and he made some promises to God. One of them was: “I will rather die than sin.”
When Dominic was twelve, he went to a school in Turin run by Saint John Bosco, a priest who taught boys who had no one to look after them. Dominic obeyed his teachers, helped younger boys with their studies, and stopped fights. He said that holiness is being very cheerful and doing small things with great love.
Dominic died when he was only fourteen. He shows us that children can be saints, and that listening to parents and teachers is one way we love God.

lessons.title: Caring for creation and for the poor
lessons.idea: We take care of the world and share with people in need. Jesus cares for the poor.
lessons.question: What can we share?
lessons.activity: Collect canned goods or toys. Plant a small plant.
teach: God asked Adam to care for the garden (Genesis 2:15; CCC 2415). We take care of creation.
Jesus said what we do for the poor, we do for him (Matthew 25:35–40; CCC 2443).
Choose a service project children can do.
talk: How can we care for the earth?
Who needs our help?
What can you share?
quiz: God asked humans to…|Ignore it|Sell it|Destroy it|Care for creation|3|Genesis 2:15.
Jesus cares for…|Nobody|Only the rich|The poor|Kings|2|Matthew 25.
Sharing is…|Boring|Silly|A way to love|Wrong|2|CCC 2447.
lessons.life: Pick up trash at the park and share a snack.
lessons.saint: Martin of Tours: a soldier who shared his cloak with a poor man on a freezing night.
lessons.mem: Whatever you did for one of the least of these, you did for me. (Matthew 25:40)
lessons.hook: Hold a small plant. “God put us in the garden to take care of it.”
lessons.assess: Ask for one way to care for creation and one to help someone in need.

script.open: Say, “It is a freezing cold day. I have a nice warm coat, and someone else has none. What should I do?” Put your coat around a child, and let the children talk about what is fair and what is kind.
teach: Say: “God made the world and gave it to us. The garden of Eden was a place to care for. The Bible says God put people in the garden ‘to till it and keep it.’ (Genesis 2:15) We are God’s helpers. We take care of the earth, the plants, the animals, the water and the air.”

Say: “Jesus also cares about people who are poor, hungry or lonely. He told a story: ‘I was hungry, and you gave me food. I was thirsty, and you gave me drink. I was a stranger, and you welcomed me.’ Then he said, ‘Whatever you did for one of the least of these, you did for me.’ (Matthew 25:35-40) When we help someone in need, we are helping Jesus.”
Say: “What can a first grader do? Pick up trash, save water, share toys, bring food for the food pantry, make a card for a lonely neighbor, pray. Small things help.”
ask: Why do we take care of the world? (God made it, and gave it to us.)
Who does Jesus say we help when we help the poor? (Jesus himself.)
What can you do to help? (Share, give, pick up litter, pray.)
practice: Collect canned goods or toys (send a note home ahead of time), or look at photos of food pantry donations.
Let children place each item into a box and say, “For Jesus.”
Plant a small seed or plant in a cup. Say, “We take care of God’s world.”
Water it and put it in a sunny place.
script.close: Pray: “Jesus, help us care for the world and for the poor.” Sign of the Cross. Send home: “Choose one thing to share with someone who needs it.”

tryit: Bring a can of food or a toy to share.
lessons.saintStory:
Martin was born around the year 316 and joined the Roman army as a young man. He was not yet baptized, but he already tried to be good.
One bitterly cold winter day, as he rode through the city gate of Amiens in France, a beggar was freezing, barely dressed. Martin had nothing to give but his own cloak. He drew his sword, cut his cloak in two, and gave half to the beggar. That night, the story goes, Martin dreamed of Jesus wearing the half cloak, saying, “Martin gave me this.”
Martin was baptized soon after and later became a monk and a bishop. He teaches what Jesus said: whatever we do for the poor, we do for him.

units.title: Praying and the Church year
units.eq: How do we pray all year?

lessons.title: Ways we pray
lessons.idea: We pray to praise God, to thank him, to ask for help and to say sorry. We can pray anywhere.
lessons.question: What do you want to tell God today?
lessons.activity: Make four prayer cards: Praise, Thanks, Please, Sorry. Pick one to pray.
teach: We pray to praise, thank, ask and say sorry (CCC 2623, 2626, 2629–2630). Psalm 100 is a song of praise.
We can pray anywhere (Philippians 4:6).
Let children pray in their own words.
talk: What do you want to thank God for?
What do you want to ask?
When do you say sorry?
quiz: A prayer of thanks says…|Thank you, God|Hello|I’m sorry|Please|0|CCC 2638.
A prayer of petition asks for…|Silence|Toys only|Help|Nothing|2|CCC 2629.
Praise says…|I’m tired|You are great, God|Give me|Go away|1|CCC 2639.
lessons.life: Pray one of each kind of prayer this week.
lessons.saint: Monica: a mother who prayed for her son for many years, and God answered.
lessons.mem: Thank you, God.
lessons.hook: Hold four cards: Praise, Thanks, Please, Sorry. “These are ways to talk to God.”
lessons.assess: Ask children to choose one card and say a prayer.

script.open: Hold up four small cards: a heart, a gift, a hand, a tear. Say, “These are four ways to talk to God. Let’s see if we can guess what each one means.” Let children guess before you explain.
teach: Say: “Prayer is talking and listening to God. You can pray anywhere: at home, in the car, in church, in bed. You can pray with your own words or with words you have learned. Here are four things we do when we pray.”

Say: “One: we praise God. Praise means telling God how wonderful he is. ‘God, you are great! You made the whole world.’ (Psalm 100.) Two: we thank God. ‘Thank you for my family. Thank you for food.’ Three: we ask God. ‘Please help my friend who is sick.’ Our asking is called a petition. Four: we say sorry. ‘God, I am sorry for what I did.’”

Say: “St. Paul said, ‘Do not worry about anything, but in everything, by prayer, with thanksgiving, make your requests known to God.’ (Philippians 4:6) We can tell God anything. He is our Father, and he loves to hear us.”
ask: What are four kinds of prayer? (Praise, thanks, please, sorry.)
When can you pray? (Any time, anywhere.)
What would you like to praise God for? (Take several.)
practice: Give each child four small cards: Praise, Thanks, Please, Sorry. Have them draw a symbol on each (a star, a gift, hands, a tear).
Mix them up, and let each child pick one card.
Ask the child to pray in their own words for that kind of prayer.
Everyone says “Amen” together after each prayer.
script.close: Say a short prayer of thanks together. Sign of the Cross. Send home: “Use the cards to pray with your family tonight.”

tryit: Choose a prayer card: Praise, Thanks, Please or Sorry.
lessons.saintStory:
