Monica was born in North Africa around the year 331. She was a Christian and married a man who was not. Her son Augustine grew up clever, but he lived a wild life and did not follow Jesus.
Monica prayed for Augustine every day, for many years. She cried and begged God to help him. She even followed him across the sea to Italy. A wise bishop told her, “It is not possible that the son of so many tears should be lost.” She kept on praying.
After about seventeen years, Augustine did turn to God, and was baptized. He became a bishop and one of the greatest saints. Monica died soon after. She teaches us to pray and never give up, because God hears us.

lessons.title: Our Father and Hail Mary
lessons.idea: Jesus gave us the Our Father. Mary prays with us when we say the Hail Mary.
lessons.question: Which prayer do you like best?
lessons.activity: Pray the Our Father and a decade of the Rosary slowly together.
teach: The Our Father is Jesus’ prayer (Matthew 6:9–13; CCC 2759). The Hail Mary has Gabriel’s and Elizabeth’s words (CCC 2676).
Pray slowly with gestures. Introduce the rosary beads.
Explain unfamiliar words.
talk: Which prayer is your favorite?
What do you ask in the Our Father?
Why do we pray the Hail Mary?
quiz: Jesus taught us…|The Hail Mary|The Gloria|The Creed|The Our Father|3|Matthew 6:9.
The Hail Mary is a prayer to…|Angels|Mary|Joseph|Peter|1|Luke 1:28.
The Rosary has…|Candles|Books|Beads|Stones|2|CCC 2678.
lessons.life: Pray a decade of the Rosary with your family.
lessons.saint: Dominic: tradition says Mary gave him the Rosary.
lessons.mem: Hail Mary, full of grace, the Lord is with thee; blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb, Jesus.
lessons.hook: Say, “Jesus taught his friends how to pray.”
lessons.assess: Ask children to pray the Our Father with you.

script.open: Show a string of rosary beads. Ask, “Has anyone seen these? What are they for?” Pass them around. “This is a special way to pray. But first, we will learn the two most important prayers.”
teach: Say: “The friends of Jesus said, ‘Lord, teach us to pray.’ And Jesus gave them the Our Father. It is the prayer of all God’s children. We pray it at Mass, at home, at school and in bed. It starts: ‘Our Father, who art in heaven’ because we are talking to God as our Father.”

Go through it in simple words: “We say his name is holy. We ask for his kingdom to come. We ask for our daily bread. We ask him to forgive us as we forgive others. We ask him to keep us safe from evil.”

Say: “The Hail Mary is the prayer we say to Mary. It starts with the angel’s greeting. When we say it, Mary prays with us. The Rosary is a prayer made of Our Fathers and Hail Marys. We use beads to count. One group of ten Hail Marys is called a decade. While we say them, we think about Jesus’ life.”
ask: Who gave us the Our Father? (Jesus.)
Who do we pray to in the Hail Mary? (Mary.)
What do the beads help us do? (Count the prayers while we think about Jesus.)
practice: Pass out a bead each (or pass around a rosary), and stand in a circle.
Pray the Our Father slowly, all together.
Pray one decade of Hail Marys together, using a rosary or counting on fingers. One child leads the first half, and the class answers the second half.
Say the Glory Be at the end.
script.close: Say the Glory Be together. Sign of the Cross. Send home: “Pray an Our Father and a Hail Mary with your family tonight.”

tryit: Pray a decade of the Rosary.
Listen to Mary praying with you.
lessons.saintStory:
Dominic Guzmán was born in Spain in about 1170. As a young man, he sold his books to feed the poor during a famine. He became a priest and spent many years traveling and preaching to people who had stopped believing in Jesus.
Dominic started a new order, the Dominicans, whose friars taught the faith to everyone. He loved to study, and he loved to pray. An old tradition says that Mary appeared to Dominic and gave him the Rosary, a way to pray with her and think about the life of Jesus, to help people who struggled to believe.
Whether that is how it started, the Rosary became a favorite prayer of the Church. Dominic shows us that praying slowly, with Mary, helps us know Jesus.

lessons.title: Advent, Christmas, Lent and Easter
lessons.idea: The Church year helps us remember Jesus. Each season has colors and signs.
lessons.question: What color do we see in Advent? In Easter?
lessons.activity: Color a church-year wheel with purple, white, green and red.
teach: The Church year helps us remember Jesus (CCC 1163, 1168–1169). Purple (Advent, Lent), white (Christmas, Easter), green (Ordinary Time), red (Pentecost, martyrs).
Connect each season to a sign: wreath, manger, ashes, candle.
Make a classroom church-year wheel.
talk: What color is Advent?
Why is Easter white?
What season are we in?
quiz: Advent is…|Red|Black|Purple|Orange|2|Liturgy.
Easter is…|Green|White|Black|Purple|1|Liturgy.
Ordinary Time is…|Green|Pink|Red|Blue|0|Liturgy.
lessons.life: Look for the color of the season on the priest’s vestments.
lessons.saint: Isidore the Farmer: a field worker who prayed through the seasons of the year.
lessons.mem: Jesus is with us all year.
lessons.hook: Show four colors: purple, white, green, red. “Each means something.”
lessons.assess: Ask children to match colors and seasons.

script.open: Bring four items: a purple cloth, a white cloth, a green cloth and a red cloth. Hold them up one by one and ask, “Have you ever seen these colors at church? When?” Let the children share what they notice.
teach: Say: “The Church has a calendar, too. It is called the liturgical year, and it helps us remember the story of Jesus, season by season. Each season has a color.”

Say: “Purple is for Advent and Lent. These are times to get ready. In Advent we get ready for Christmas, and in Lent we get ready for Easter. White (or gold) is for Christmas and Easter, the happiest times. Green is for Ordinary Time, when we grow. Red is for the Holy Spirit, and for martyrs, who gave their lives for Jesus.”

Say: “Through the whole year, we can remember that Jesus is with us. The colors and signs, like the Advent wreath, the Christmas crib, ashes, the palms and the Easter candle, are like pictures to help us remember.”
ask: What color is used for Advent and Lent? (Purple.)
What color is used at Christmas and Easter? (White or gold.)
What does green mean? (Growing, Ordinary Time.)
practice: Give each child a circle divided into four or five pie pieces. Label them: Advent, Christmas, Lent, Easter, Ordinary Time.
Help children color each part: purple, white, purple, white, green.
Have children say a sentence about each season: “In Advent, we wait. At Christmas, Jesus is born.”
Hang the wheels up to look at throughout the year.
script.close: Pray: “Jesus, be with us all year.” Sign of the Cross. Send home: “Look at the color the priest wears this Sunday.”

lessons.saintStory:
Isidore was born in Madrid, Spain, around the year 1070. His family was poor, and he grew up to be a farmworker, plowing, sowing and harvesting for a wealthy landowner.
Isidore went to Mass every morning before work, and he prayed as he worked in the fields. The other workers complained that he was late, but the landowner saw that Isidore’s work always got done. Legend says that angels plowed for him while he prayed. He and his wife, María, were generous, and they shared their food with the poor, even when they had little.
Isidore is the patron of farmers. He teaches us that each season, in the fields and in the church year, is a time to pray, work and thank God.
